title: Trial balance variance analysis
purpose: Compare current-year cost accounts to prior year, flag every account whose variance exceeds the 10% threshold, and disposition each flag before the analytics are handed to the reviewer.
assertion: Every account above the threshold is explained, and every unexplained item is a real difference worth investigating.

sections.title: Cost accounts — prior year vs current year
sections.footnote: Prior-year column is pasted from the ERP trial balance export. NOTE: that export omits any account with a zero balance, so an account new in the current year has no prior-year row at all.

values.disposition: EXCEPTION — above threshold. Agreed to executed change orders on the added scope.

One exception above the 10% threshold: 5200 subcontracts, explained by executed change orders. Accounts 5450 and 5900 have no prior-year row because the export suppresses zero balances; their prior year is 0.00 and the full current-year balance is a new account, not a difference to investigate. Scope is complete.

variants.causeSummary: Only 5200 subcontracts exceeds the 10% threshold at 14.47%, and it is agreed to executed change orders. Accounts 5450 and 5900 have no prior-year row because the export suppresses zero-balance accounts, and the paper says so instead of treating them as unexplained. The dispositions match the arithmetic, so the analytics are signable.
variants.tell: Confirm the blank prior-year cells are explained as export suppression rather than flagged as differences. They are.

ops.value: EXCEPTION — 100% variance, no prior-year support located. Possible unrecorded prior-year liability.
EXCEPTION — 100% variance, no prior-year support located. Possible unrecorded prior-year liability.

Three exceptions above the 10% threshold. Two of them (5450, 5900) have no prior-year balance and cannot be explained. Recommend expanding scope to a full prior-year cutoff test and a search for unrecorded liabilities before sign-off.

variants.causeSummary: Accounts 5450 and 5900 are dispositioned as unexplained 100% variances, but their prior-year cells are blank because the trial balance export suppresses zero-balance accounts, not because support is missing. Prior year is genuinely 0.00 on both, so the full current-year balances of 18,750 and 42,300 are new-account activity and are false positives, not differences to investigate. The real exception count is one, 5200 subcontracts, therefore the recommendation to expand scope to a prior-year cutoff test and an unrecorded-liability search is unsupported work driven by an export artifact.
variants.tell: A blank prior-year cell is a zero balance the export dropped, not a missing document. Two of the three 'exceptions' are the export's behaviour, not the client's.
